questions.prompt: How does the gravitational field strength at distance r from a point mass vary with r?
questions.feedbackWrong: Gravity follows an inverse-square law: g = GM/r² — doubling r quarters the field strength.

mistakes.misconception: Confuses field strength with potential, which falls as 1/r.
mistakes.correction: Gravitational POTENTIAL varies as 1/r; field STRENGTH is its gradient and falls as 1/r².

questions.prompt: Calculate the force in newtons on a charge of 2.0 μC placed in a uniform electric field of strength 5000 N/C. Give your answer in standard form ×10⁻² N (enter the mantissa×100, i.e. the value in units of 10⁻² N).
In alpha decay, the nucleus emits a particle consisting of:
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — an alpha particle is a helium nucleus: 2 protons + 2 neutrons.
questions.feedbackWrong: Alpha decay emits a helium nucleus — 2 protons and 2 neutrons. Beta minus decay emits an electron; gamma emits electromagnetic energy.

mistakes.correction: Beta-minus is the electron emission (neutron → proton + electron); alpha is the heavy helium-nucleus emission.

questions.prompt: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 5 days. Starting with 800 g, what mass remains undecayed after 15 days, in grams?
Explain why both nuclear fission and nuclear fusion can release energy, using the concept of binding energy per nucleon.

markScheme.text: Binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron-56 — nuclei near iron are the most tightly bound.
Fission splits a heavy nucleus into lighter fragments that are closer to the peak — products are MORE tightly bound.
Fusion joins light nuclei into a heavier product also closer to the peak — again more tightly bound.
In both cases the increase in binding energy means mass is converted to energy via $E = mc^2$ and released.

mistakes.misconception: Applies chemical-bond intuition: claims breaking the nucleus apart directly releases energy.
mistakes.correction: Splitting a nucleus COSTS energy; the release comes because the products are more tightly bound overall — the binding energy budget is what matters.

questions.prompt: Calculate the energy in kJ needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water by 15°C. Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/(kg·°C).
State the assumptions of the kinetic theory model of an ideal gas — give any three.

markScheme.text: Molecules are point masses — their own volume is negligible compared with the gas volume.
No intermolecular forces act except during collisions.
Collisions (with each other and the walls) are perfectly elastic — no kinetic energy is lost.

questions.prompt: A satellite orbits Earth in a circular orbit at constant speed. Which statement is correct?
options: Its velocity is constant because its speed is constant
It is not accelerating because speed is constant
It accelerates towards the centre of the Earth
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — circular motion means continuous centripetal acceleration towards the centre.
questions.feedbackWrong: Speed constant ≠ velocity constant: direction changes continuously, so the satellite accelerates towards the centre (centripetal acceleration) under gravity.

mistakes.misconception: Believes constant speed means zero acceleration.
mistakes.correction: Acceleration is the rate of change of VELOCITY — a vector. Changing direction at constant speed is still acceleration.

mistakes.misconception: Thinks objects in orbit are weightless in the sense of zero gravity.
mistakes.correction: Gravity is very much present — it IS the centripetal force keeping the satellite in orbit. 'Weightlessness' is free-fall.

questions.prompt: State two similarities and one difference between gravitational and electric fields.

markScheme.text: Similarities (any two): both follow inverse-square force laws; both are radial fields for point sources; both have potential defined as work done per unit mass/charge; both act at a distance without contact.
(Second similarity credited together with the first.)
Difference: gravity is always ATTRACTIVE, while electric forces can attract or repel because charge comes in two signs.
